title: Global Hub Navigation: proposal + grooming notes
content:
Summary:
This note captures a focused proposal for a single "global hub" navigation model for the Redwood Console plus a prioritized grooming list to convert the proposal into deliverable tickets. Goal is to reduce cognitive overhead across product areas, make routing predictable for integrations (hosted/dedicated/private), and provide space for platform + tenant-specific actions without proliferating isolated nav patterns.

Design goals (top-level):
- Predictable URL structure (resource-first) so engineers can hard-link pages and tests reliably.
- Clear separation between global workspace-level controls and model/deployment artifacts.
- Minimize depth: aim for 2–3 levels of nav.
- Graceful collapse for left rail (compact + full) and a top-level breadcrumb for deep contexts.
- Accessibility + keyboard-first nav (ARIA roles, focus trapping during modals).

Constraints / non-goals:
- This doc does not define visual theming or final copy; those are follow-ups.
- No heavy changes to role-based access control (RBAC) behavior yet — keep existing permissions surface.
- We avoid changing the billing dashboard in this pass (separate product work).

Proposed information architecture (flat-list, top -> children):
1. Home (workspace overview)
2. Projects (list of projects / tenant-like grouping)
   - Project overview
   - Models (catalog + versioning)
   - Deployments (active endpoints, pools)
   - Routes (per-route config, rollouts)
3. Experiments (evaluations, prompt tests)
4. Observability
   - Metrics
   - Traces
   - Logs
5. Capacity (Dedicated pools + scaling rules)
6. Security & Keys (KMS, API keys, audit logs)
7. Settings (org-wide + project switcher)
8. Help & Support (quick links, docs, contact)

Notes on grouping rationale:
- Models and Deployments are siblings under Projects to emphasize model lifecycle -> serving path.
- Routes are surfaced as a first-class node because rollouts/fallback policies are frequently edited by platform teams.
- Observability is kept distinct (not nested under Deployments) so users can quickly look across projects.

Sidebar behavior states:
- Expanded (default for desktop): shows icons + labels, primary groups separated by dividers.
- Compact (user toggled): icons only, tooltips on hover, top left shows project selector reduced to an avatar + caret.
- Pinned mode: user can pin a subset of items (Models, Deployments, Routes) into a quick-access rail.
- Mobile: collapse to bottom sheet with 5 primary actions (Home, Projects, Experiments, Observability, Help).

Routing and URL patterns (proposal):
- /workspace/:workspaceId/ -> Home overview for workspace
- /workspace/:workspaceId/project/:projectId -> Project overview (canonical)
- /workspace/:workspaceId/project/:projectId/models -> Models list
- /workspace/:workspaceId/project/:projectId/models/:modelId -> Model detail (versions tab selected via query param)
- /workspace/:workspaceId/project/:projectId/deployments -> Deployments list
- /workspace/:workspaceId/project/:projectId/deployments/:deploymentId
- /workspace/:workspaceId/observability/metrics?project=:projectId&range=24h

Routing rules:
- All canonical pages must be reachable via direct URL (no client-only ephemeral state).
- When switching project from a page that does not exist in the destination project (e.g., modelId not present), fallback to project overview and surface a toast: "Item not found in target project — switched to overview."

Wireframe sketches (conceptual):
- Left rail (vertical) with three visual tiers: workspace selector (top), primary nav, secondary utilities (bottom: keys, billing, support).
- Mid-column: page title, breadcrumbs (workspace > project > area), page-level actions to the right (Create, Import, Quick Actions).
- Right rail (optional): contextual quick-help and last 5 activity events (collapsible).

Microcopy examples (to standardize tone):
- Project selector placeholder: "Select a project — your models and deployments live here."
- Models list CTA: "Add model" / "Import checkpoint"
- Deployment empty state: "No active endpoints. Create a deployment to serve this model in production."

Accessibility notes:
- Sidebar must use role="navigation" and skip links to main content.
- Keyboard nav: Up/Down to traverse items, Enter to open, Space to toggle pin.
- Ensure contrast ratios meet WCAG AA for icons + labels.

Performance implications:
- Avoid client-side full nav recompute on every websocket update from observability streams.
- Prefetch lightweight metadata for the first two depths only (workspace and project lists). Defer heavy model metadata until detail view is requested.

Grooming backlog (prioritized):
- RH-2142 (P0) Global hub routing skeleton: implement URL structure + project switching behavior. Est: 5 pts. Acceptance: all routes listed above return valid pages (mock data allowed).
- RH-2179 (P0) Left rail component (expanded/compact/pinned) with keyboard controls. Est: 8 pts. Acceptance: toggle persists per-user; keyboard nav passes basic e2e.
- RH-2211 (P1) Project selector UX + empty-state flows. Est: 3 pts. Acceptance: project switch sends analytics event and respects RBAC fallbacks.
- RH-2234 (P1) Observability top-level page + cross-project metrics filter. Est: 5 pts. Acceptance: metrics filter works via query params and deep-links.
- RH-2250 (P2) Right rail activity feed component (collapsible). Est: 3 pts. Acceptance: shows last 5 events, collapsible state persisted.

Each ticket should include a small acceptance checklist (example for RH-2179):
- keyboard navigation implemented (unit + e2e)
- compact mode hides labels and shows tooltips on hover
- pinned items persist to user preferences API
- visual QA signoff from design

Open questions for the next sync (design + eng):
1) Do we expose routes as first-class nav for non-admin users? pros: faster rollouts; cons: more surface area.
2) How do we represent cross-workspace resources (if we need to in future)? recommended: explicit "Global" workspace instead of mixing.
3) Should the breadcrumb show truncated names with hover tooltip or an overflow menu for very deep names?

Analytics and success metrics (initial):
- Decrease mean time-to-find (MTTF) for common tasks (create deployment, edit route) measured via event funnels by 20% quarter-over-quarter.
- Reduce project-switch failure rate to <1% (users landing on 404s after switching).
- Adoption: target 70% of active users using compact/pinned modes within 6 weeks of rollout.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (canary): implement routes + left rail skeleton behind a feature flag for internal teams.
- Phase 1 (beta): open to 10% of customers with opt-in, collect qualitative feedback via in-app survey.
- Phase 2 (gradual): default rollout with analytics monitoring and gradual ramp if error budgets allow.

Next steps / owners:
- Engineering: RH-2142 owner: Ethan Rivera — spike to implement route resolver by 2026-03-01.
- Design: Lina Gomez — produce high-fidelity left-rail comps for expanded/compact/pinned by 2026-02-28.
- PM: Marcus Patel — consolidate feedback and open tickets (this doc -> Linear).

Appendix: Quick dev notes for implementation
- Use nested routes but avoid dynamic client-only segments; prefer paramized routes (see routing patterns above).
- Persist user rail preferences in /api/v1/user/preferences with small payload {"navMode":"compact","pinned":["models","deployments"]} (backend ticket separate).
- Provide an admin-only toggle in settings to revert to legacy nav during rollout.

End of notes.

(Recorded sync: slack thread https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1643209352000, design comps in Confluence link above.)
